html:
The kafala system is the sponsorship system under which millions of migrant workers have come to the Gulf since the oil boom of the 1970s. Each worker's visa and right to stay is tied to a sponsor, usually the employer.

The UAE is the most extreme case: close to nine in ten of its residents are foreigners, most from India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal and the Philippines. They built Dubai and Abu Dhabi and run their hospitals, shops and homes, while sending money back to families in South Asia.

Because the sponsor controls the right to change jobs or leave, rights groups have long criticised the system for abuse and debt bondage. Several Gulf states have reformed it in recent years. Compare Saudi Arabia and Qatar, which use the same system.
sum: The kafala system is the sponsorship system under which millions of migrant workers have come to the Gulf since the oil boom of the 1970s. Each worker's visa and right to stay is tied to a sponsor, usually the employer.
